metadata.note: The Minneapolis and St. Louis Railway - 'the Louie', the Albert Lea Route and Peoria Gateway - and the companies that ran its Iowa lines before it: the Central Railroad of Iowa, Central Iowa Railway and Iowa Central Railway (absorbed 1 Jan 1912), and the Des Moines and Fort Dodge. Drawn from research/branches/minneapolis_and_st_louis_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains) (2026-10-05). Before this layer the map drew no M&StL route at all. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn, which keep to years a source confirms. The M&StL's last passenger train, Minneapolis - Watertown Nos. 13/14, arrived on 21 July 1960; the Chicago and North Western bought the road on 1 Nov 1960, after it, so no C&NW-coloured successor feature is drawn. Rule 4 splits: Central Railroad of Iowa -> Central Iowa (18 June 1879) -> Iowa Central (16 May 1889) -> M&StL (1 Jan 1912), and Des Moines & Fort Dodge (to c. Apr 1887) -> M&StL (1 Jan 1905). The 1881 consolidation, the receiverships and the 1894, 1916 and 1939-43 reorganisations are the same operator and share one colour, as do the Minnesota, Dakota & Pacific and Iowa Central & Western construction companies. Track the M&StL used under trackage rights (BCR&N/Rock Island at Albert Lea - Northwood, Rock Island at Gowrie - Des Moines, Illinois Central at Fort Dodge) is drawn in M&StL colour because the M&StL ran these trains.

The Peoria mixed's end is the biggest open question (an unverified source says 1954). Hofsommer's 'The Tootin' Louie' (2005) and Classic Trains Summer 2010 ('M&StL's Story City branch') are the likely sources.

Start years that are the first CONFIRMED year, not the opening ([OPEN]): Minneapolis - Hopkins - Merriam 1874, Merriam - Albert Lea 1881, Albert Lea - Fort Dodge 1881, Mason City - Albia 1875, Peoria line 1893, Story City Branch 1882.

The exact junctions of the 1935 Peoria-line realignment onto the ex-CB&Q Martinsburg - Packwood - Brighton line.

Who ran the Des Moines & Fort Dodge's trains 1887-1904 is the Rock Island, but no dated Rock Island-run train was found, so that era is not drawn. A 1896 M&StL through car ran Angus - Des Moines over it (DONOVAN) and could be drawn as an M&StL anchor.

Spencer - Ruthven - Gilmore City - Tara: no dated passenger year; OG1952 Table 4 freight only.
